prompt.en: Explain how the ziggurat was both the religious centre and the centre of power in a Sumerian city-state. Give five points.

label.en: It was the temple of the city's chief god, and the whole city grew outward from it

level1.en: Why does one building end up at the centre of the whole city?

clue.en: The ziggurat was built for the city's chief god, and the city grew around it.

level2Template.en: The ziggurat served as the temple of the city's ___, and the city grew around it.

label.en: Farming, trade and the transport of goods were all tied to the temple authority

level1.en: Who was actually managing the farming, trade and craft production going on around the ziggurat?

clue.en: Farming, trade and the transport of goods were all tied to the temple authority.

level2Template.en: Much of the city's ___ was tied directly to temple authority.

label.en: It served as the city's treasury, with royal storehouses around it, which is why the walls had only one entrance

level1.en: The walls had only one entrance. What was being kept safe behind them?

clue.en: It served as the city's treasury, so the walls around it had only one entrance.

level2Template.en: It held royal storehouses and served as a ___, which explains the single entrance.

label.en: Restricted entry marks a ruling group of priests, and a society divided into ranks

level1.en: If almost nobody was allowed to climb to the summit, what does that say about who was allowed to?

clue.en: Only high priests and priestesses could enter, and they were probably part of the ruling class. This shows a society divided into ranks.

level2Template.en: Restricted entry to the temple shows a ruling group of priests and a ___.

label.en: Worship, wealth and power met in one place

level1.en: Worship, wealth and control of the city's work: did these sit in different places, or in one?

clue.en: Worship, the city's wealth and control of its work all met at the temple.

level2Template.en: Ultimately, this shows religion and government working as a ___.
